name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
description: VoiceAssistant-Eval is a comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. It comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories, including natural sounds, music, and spoken dialogue for listening; multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and various scenarios for speaking; and highly heterogeneous images for viewing. The benchmark evaluates 21 open-source models and GPT-4o-Audio, measuring the quality of response content and speech, as well as their consistency.
creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li (CUHK MMLab, SenseTime Research, CPII under InnoHK)
citeAs: Wang et al., VoiceAssistant-Eval: Benchmarking AI Assistants Across Listening, Speaking, and Viewing
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from 47 source datasets spanning audio understanding, speech, music, and vision domains. Text instructions were converted to audio using TTS models. For role-playing, 100 distinct roles were selected and three representative audio clips per role were collected. Speech instructions were synthesized using three advanced TTS models (F5TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B) and evaluated with UTMOS, regenerating any clips scoring below 3.8. Synthesized audio was transcribed with Whisper-Large-v3 and only recordings with the lowest word error rates were retained.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Approximately 10% of candidates were removed during curation due to missing or broken audio or images, as well as instances with ill-posed questions or incorrect answers.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source data was extracted from 47 datasets including: MMMU, VocalBench, AlpacaEval, MMSU, RoleBench, AdvBench, AIR-Bench, MEAD, BeaverTails-Eval, MT-Bench-101, VCTK, IFEval, MusicCaps, CommonVoice, SD-Eval, Nsynth, BIG-Bench Hard, Clotho, SLURP, VoiceBench, MTJ-Jamendo, JL Corpus, MELD, AudioCaps, AudioGrounding, CoVoST 2, LibriSpeech, VocalSound, VoxCeleb1, MUSIA-AVQA, FoR, SpeechInstructBench, IEMOCAP, FollowBench, SpokenWOZ, TUT2017, AVQA, CommonsenseQA, GSM8K, STORAL, Clotho-AQA, FMA, CochlScene, Fisher, MT Bench, RAVDESS, MyST.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Text instructions were preprocessed for TTS synthesis: special image reference tokens were replaced with descriptive phrases; text was rewritten using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct to ensure numbers and mathematical expressions are read accurately; multiple-choice question options were rephrased for better readability. Speech was synthesized using F5TTS, ChatTTS, and Dia-1.6B, evaluated with UTMOS Strong (threshold 3.8), and transcribed with Whisper-Large-v3 to select the lowest WER audio.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A four-stage curation process was applied: (1) Deduplication using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance, with manual review and removal of suspected duplicates, resulting in 15,359 samples; (2) Validation to exclude incomplete or unsuitable instances including corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and incorrect answers (approximately 10% discarded); (3) Categorization of remaining problems into 13 predefined task categories based on source metadata; (4) Balanced sampling to equalize category representation, yielding 10,497 final samples.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Model responses are evaluated across three dimensions: (1) Content quality: assessed using gpt-oss-20b with thirteen task-specific evaluator prompts; for emotion tasks, emotion2vec is used to get emotion probabilities. (2) Speech quality: measured using UTMOS providing fluency and naturalness scores. (3) Consistency: computed via modified Word Error Rate between Whisper-Large-v3 transcriptions and model text responses. For role-play tasks, Wespeaker is used to calculate speaker similarity between model-generated speech and reference role audio. Human evaluation was conducted on 10% of Qwen2.5-Omni-7B responses (1,050 examples) across 13 tasks for validation.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A lightweight web-based curation tool was built for manual quality checks. Curators reviewed each item on a single screen with inline audio players, image viewers, transcripts, and multiple-choice options, assigning Good or Bad verdicts with optional notes.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation validation showed Pearson correlation coefficients between gpt-oss-20b automated scores and human ratings ranging from 0.73 to 1.00 (overall 0.92), with agreement rates uniformly above 90% and an overall agreement rate of 96.1%. Evaluation stability was assessed by repeating scoring ten times on 10% of samples, showing low variance (standard deviations mostly below 3). Statistical significance testing used paired two-sided t-tests with Bonferroni correction.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: gpt-oss-20b (content quality evaluation), UTMOS Strong / UTMOS (speech quality evaluation), Whisper-Large-v3 (speech transcription and WER computation), emotion2vec (emotion probability estimation), Wespeaker (speaker similarity for role-play tasks), F5TTS / ChatTTS / Dia-1.6B (speech synthesis for question audio), Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (text rewriting for TTS preprocessing)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and evaluation code will be publicly released under an MIT license. The authors bear all responsibility in case of violation of rights. A data governance process for auditing and removal is maintained, with the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation using audio clips from 100 distinct roles (including 5 Chinese roles). Speaker audio profiles are used for voice personalization evaluation. The authors emphasize strict consent, provenance, and anti-impersonation safeguards, prohibiting training or releasing models intended to reproduce identifiable speakers without documented consent.
rai:dataSocialImpact: VoiceAssistant-Eval is intended to push the boundaries of AI assistant capabilities and facilitate development of next-generation multimodal models. It has applications in healthcare, education, smart homes, customer service, and automotive industries. The benchmark identifies gaps in safety alignment and robustness, and includes safety evaluation tasks. Anti-impersonation safeguards are included to mitigate misuse risks such as identity spoofing, harassment, and fraud. The authors require downstream users to implement consent gating and watermarking of synthetic audio.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset has a monolingual focus (primarily English, with only 5 Chinese roles in role-play), which may not capture the full variability of real user interactions and may not generalize to diverse linguistic settings. Questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources, which might not reflect the full richness or fairness concerns of real deployments. The role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles that may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas. The benchmark may carry biases from its source data and design choices.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset (10.5K items) may be limited in diversity and has a monolingual (English) focus. The range of evaluated models is limited, with only one proprietary system (GPT-4o-Audio). Evaluation relies on automated measures and GPT-based scoring, which may introduce noise and bias. Video-audio integration and continuous audio-visual streaming tasks are not covered. The benchmark evaluates models in an offline, static manner and does not measure latency, partial utterance handling, barge-in, or error recovery. The benchmark is not supposed to be used for training models for cheating.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating and benchmarking voice AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities. It is designed for Testing and Evaluation use cases. Researchers should use this dataset to better evaluate voice assistants and facilitate future studies. It is not intended for training models to cheat on the benchmark.
